Aircraft.title: Aircraft
Aircraft.description: Makes the object fly: lift, drag and thrust computed on its own motion, and control surfaces that only answer with air over them.

Animator.title: Animator
Animator.description: Plays the clip that matches what the body is doing — walking, jumping, standing — from an animation graph of the project.

CharacterController.description: Makes the object the one being driven: it walks, it jumps, it climbs steps.
CharacterController.title: Character

Collider.description: Gives the object a volume the others cannot pass through.
Collider.title: Volume

Follow.description: Follows another entity and stops at the distance asked for — a companion, a shoulder camera, an enemy.
Follow.title: Chase

Health.description: Hit points, which fall as the entity is hurt and kill it at zero.
Health.title: Health

LookAt.description: Points the entity at another one, at once or at a capped turning speed — a turret, a sign, a head.
LookAt.title: Gaze

Movement.description: Makes the entity travel on its own along one axis — a platform, a lift, a hazard.
Movement.title: Motion

Orbit.description: Turns the entity about another one, or about the origin — a moon, a satellite, a circling camera.
Orbit.title: Orbit

Path.description: Walks the entity along a run of points at a steady pace — a cart, a dolly shot, a platform on rails.
Path.title: Rail

Patrol.description: Walks the entity from one named point to the next, waiting at each — a sentry, a lift.
Patrol.title: Patrol

RigidBody.description: Hands the object to the simulation: it falls, it slides, it gets pushed.
RigidBody.title: Physics

Script.title: Script
Script.description: Hands the object to code: what its author wrote runs on every step.

Player.title: Player
Player.description: Names whoever is played. One per scene: what hangs under it is its body and its eye, and it is what the camera follows.

Spin.description: Turns the entity about one axis, endlessly — a pickup, a propeller, a mechanism.
Spin.title: Spin

SpringArm.title: Spring arm
SpringArm.description: Hangs a camera behind an element at a distance you set: it pulls in when a wall comes between them, and follows with lag rather than sticking.

Trigger.description: Blocks nothing, and says so when something enters its volume or leaves it.
Trigger.title: Sensor

Vehicle.title: Vehicle
Vehicle.description: Puts the object on suspended, driven, steered wheels: it rolls, brakes and turns. The wheels are its child objects, named here.

help.id: The context’s name — what a script pushes, and what the built-in fallback completes. It comes from the file name; two files carrying one identifier would make a single context.
help.priority: Who wins when two active contexts declare the same action. The HIGHER number writes last and takes it. The built-in character, vehicle and flight contexts sit at 0, 10 and 10.
help.defaultActive: Whether this map is in service from the start of a game. Otherwise a script has to push it — a menu context opens and closes that way.
help.actionId: The name a script reads, and the built-in controllers with it: `move`, `jump`, `steer`. That name is what counts, never the key.
help.actionKind: What the action answers: a button answers yes or no, one axis answers a number between −1 and 1, two axes answer a pair — what a stick says.
help.device: Where the control comes from. One action may carry several: that is how a game answers a keyboard AND a gamepad without knowing which spoke.
help.axis: Which of the two halves this key pushes on. A two-axis action is made of four keys, two per axis.
help.scale: How far this binding pushes, and which way. −1 for the half that goes left or backwards, 1 for the other.
help.deadZone: Below this value the stick counts as at rest. A worn stick drifts: with no dead zone, the character walks off on its own.
help.invert: Turns this control round. What some pilots expect of pitch, and nobody of anything else.
